title: Linux disk appears full
summary: Distinguish exhausted filesystem blocks, inode exhaustion, deleted-but-open files, and misleading mount assumptions before changing data.

limitations: Filesystem tools and reserved-space behavior vary by filesystem and operating system.
This journey does not inspect a live host or decide what data is safe to delete.

whatItDoesNotProve: A full-looking filesystem does not identify which data is safe to remove.
An application error may refer to a different mount or inode exhaustion rather than byte capacity.

title: Docker container exits immediately
summary: Use container state, exit code, logs, and configured process evidence to distinguish expected completion from startup failure.

limitations: Logging-driver configuration can limit available logs.
Orchestrators and Compose may add restart or dependency behavior not visible from one container.

whatItDoesNotProve: A stopped container is not necessarily broken; one-shot jobs can complete successfully.
A restart policy does not fix the process or configuration that caused an unexpected exit.

title: Kubernetes Pod remains Pending
summary: Use Pod scheduling events and related evidence to distinguish resource, placement, storage, port, and scheduler constraints.

limitations: Managed platforms may add provider-specific scheduler messages.
Custom schedulers can produce different evidence.
No cluster-side, admission, or CRD validation is performed.

whatItDoesNotProve: Pending does not by itself identify one cause.
A scheduler event describes a current scheduling barrier but may not reveal every policy or provider constraint.

title: Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff
summary: Determine why a container repeatedly exits before changing probes, resources, commands, or restart behavior.

limitations: Managed platforms and runtimes may add provider-specific evidence.
No live cluster, admission, or CRD validation is performed.

whatItDoesNotProve: CrashLoopBackOff is a backoff condition, not the root cause.
A running container does not prove application health.

title: Terraform state-lock failure
summary: Determine whether a lock is active, stale, backend-specific, or caused by connectivity before any unlock.

limitations: Recovery differs by backend.
No state, run, or backend is inspected.

whatItDoesNotProve: A lock error does not prove a stale lock.
Lock age alone does not prove no run is active.

title: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway
summary: Identify the gateway that generated the 502, then inspect the immediately upstream hop.

limitations: Products may use 502 for implementation-specific failures.
No proxy, DNS, TLS or application is inspected.

whatItDoesNotProve: A 502 does not prove the application is fully offline.
It is distinct from 503 and 504.
firstChecks: Test the immediate upstream from that environment

title: Docker disk usage excessive
summary: Separate host filesystem, Docker data-root, images, containers, build cache, volumes and logs before pruning.

limitations: Docker Desktop/VM storage may release host space differently.
No daemon is inspected and volume data importance is unknown.

whatItDoesNotProve: Reclaimable does not mean unimportant.
Host usage may be outside Docker.

title: systemd service will not start
summary: Use service state, journal, effective unit and dependencies before restarting or weakening controls.

limitations: Distribution packaging, names and security controls vary.
No host or app config is inspected.

whatItDoesNotProve: Failed state is not necessarily the root cause.
reset-failed clears state/counters only.

title: Git push rejected or non-fast-forward
summary: Inspect repository identity and divergence before integrating or rewriting shared history.

reviewedAgainst: Current stable command-line behavior and official operational guidance
limitations: Server policies and hosting platforms vary.
This journey does not resolve repository permissions or execute Git commands.

whatItDoesNotProve: The symptom alone does not identify one root cause.
HelpDevOps does not inspect or change a live environment.

title: Jenkins agent is offline

reviewedAgainst: Current stable command-line behavior and official operational guidance
limitations: Plugins and managed agent providers can add launch-specific behavior.
This journey does not access a Jenkins controller or agent.

whatItDoesNotProve: The symptom alone does not identify one root cause.
HelpDevOps does not inspect or change a live environment.
firstChecks: Check the agent process and network path

reviewedAgainst: Current stable command-line behavior and official operational guidance
limitations: Resolver tools and configuration differ by platform.

whatItDoesNotProve: The symptom alone does not identify one root cause.
HelpDevOps does not inspect or change a live environment.
firstChecks: Test the resolver from the failing execution context
Confirm the queried name and record type
